summary.en: A game loop runs continuously during gameplay: each turn it processes input without blocking, updates the game state, and renders. By tracking the passage of time, it decouples the progression of game time from user input and processor speed.
summary.zh: 游戏循环在游戏运行期间持续运转：每一轮都以非阻塞方式处理输入、更新游戏状态并进行渲染。它通过追踪时间的流逝，把游戏时间的推进与用户输入和处理器速度解耦。

title.en: Decouple game time from input and CPU speed
title.zh: 让游戏时间与输入和 CPU 速度解耦

body.en: The intent of the Game Loop pattern is to decouple the progression of game time from user input and processor speed. The game should keep advancing without waiting for the player, and it should advance at the same pace no matter how fast the hardware is.
body.zh: 游戏循环模式的意图是：把游戏时间的推进与用户输入和处理器速度解耦。游戏应当在不等待玩家的情况下持续推进，并且无论硬件快慢，都以相同的节奏推进。

body.en: Early programs worked like a dishwasher: you dumped code in, pushed a button, waited, and got results out. These batch mode programs stop once the work is done. Shell scripts and command-line tools are still batch programs today.
body.zh: 早期的程序就像洗碗机：把代码放进去，按下按钮，等待，然后取出结果。这类批处理程序在工作完成后就结束了。如今的 shell 脚本和命令行工具仍然是批处理程序。

title.zh: 交互式程序会等待输入

body.en: Programmers wanted immediate feedback, so interactive programs were born, and some of the first were games like Colossal Cave Adventure. The program waits for your command, responds, and then waits again; while it is your turn, it sits there doing nothing.
body.zh: 程序员希望获得即时反馈，于是诞生了交互式程序，其中最早的一批就是像《巨洞冒险》（Colossal Cave Adventure）这样的游戏。程序等待你的指令，作出回应，然后再次等待；轮到你操作时，它什么也不做。

title.en: Event loops block, but games must keep moving
title.zh: 事件循环会阻塞，但游戏必须持续运动

body.en: GUI applications run an event loop that waits for input events such as clicks and key presses and then dispatches them. Unlike most software, games keep moving even when the user provides no input: animations play and monsters keep attacking. "Idle" events are too rudimentary for games, so the first key part of a game loop is that it processes input but doesn't wait for it.
body.zh: 图形界面程序运行一个事件循环：等待点击、按键等输入事件，然后分发它们。与大多数软件不同，即使用户没有任何输入，游戏也要继续运行：动画在播放，怪物在继续攻击。“空闲”（idle）事件对游戏来说过于简陋，所以游戏循环的第一个关键点是：它处理输入，但不等待输入。

body.en: One crank of the game loop is called a "tick" or "frame", and measuring how fast the loop cycles in real time gives frames per second (FPS). With a loop that spins as fast as it can, the frame rate depends on two factors: how much work each frame does, and the speed of the underlying platform.
body.zh: 游戏循环转动一次称为一个“tick”或“帧”（frame）；用真实时间衡量循环的转速，就得到每秒帧数（FPS）。如果循环尽可能快地运转，帧率取决于两个因素：每帧要做多少工作，以及底层平台的速度。

title.en: Running at a consistent speed on any hardware
title.zh: 在任何硬件上以一致的速度运行

body.en: Old games for fixed hardware like the NES did just enough work per frame, so on faster or slower machines they sped up or slowed down — hence the "turbo" button on old PCs. Today developers rarely know the exact hardware, so the second key job of a game loop is to run the game at a consistent speed despite hardware differences.
body.zh: 为 NES 这类固定硬件编写的老游戏每帧只做恰好足够的工作，所以换到更快或更慢的机器上，游戏本身就会变快或变慢——这就是老式 PC 上有“turbo”按钮的原因。如今开发者很少能确切知道目标硬件，所以游戏循环的第二个关键职责是：无论硬件差异如何，都让游戏以一致的速度运行。

body.en: A game loop runs continuously during gameplay. Each turn of the loop, it processes user input without blocking, updates the game state, and renders the game. It tracks the passage of time to control the rate of gameplay.
body.zh: 游戏循环在游戏过程中持续运行。循环的每一轮都以非阻塞的方式处理用户输入、更新游戏状态并渲染游戏。它追踪时间的流逝，以此控制游戏的运行速率。

title.en: You will almost certainly use it

body.en: Unlike most patterns, the author is confident you will use this one. If you use a game engine you won't write it yourself, but it is still there. Even turn-based games need it, because animation and music keep running while the game waits for your turn.
body.zh: 与大多数模式不同，作者确信你一定会用到这个模式。如果使用游戏引擎，你不必自己编写它，但它依然存在。即便是回合制游戏也需要它，因为在等待你行动时，动画和音乐仍在继续。

body.en: For the author, the game loop marks the difference between an "engine" and a "library". With a library, you own the main game loop and call into the library. An engine owns the loop and calls into your code.
body.zh: 在作者看来，游戏循环正是“引擎”和“库”的区别所在：使用库时，你掌控主游戏循环并调用库；而引擎掌控循环，并调用你的代码。

body.en: The game loop is some of the most important code in your game. If a program spends 90% of its time in 10% of the code, the game loop is firmly in that 10%, so be careful with it and mindful of its efficiency.
body.zh: 游戏循环是整个游戏中最重要的代码之一。如果说程序 90% 的时间花在 10% 的代码上，那么游戏循环必然属于那 10%，所以要谨慎对待它，并留意它的效率。

title.en: Coordinating with the platform's event loop
title.zh: 与平台的事件循环协调

subsection.en: You may need to coordinate with the platform's event loop
subsection.zh: 你可能需要与平台的事件循环协调

body.en: On a platform with its own GUI event loop, two application loops are in play and must cooperate. On Windows you can make your loop the only one and call PeekMessage(), which, unlike GetMessage(), doesn't block. In a web browser the event loop is built into the execution model, so you use it as your game loop via something like requestAnimationFrame().
body.zh: 如果平台自带图形界面和事件循环，就会同时存在两个应用循环，它们必须和平相处。在 Windows 上，你可以让自己的循环成为唯一的循环，并调用 PeekMessage()——与 GetMessage() 不同，它不会阻塞。而在网页浏览器中，事件循环深植于执行模型之中，你只能把它当作游戏循环来用，例如通过 requestAnimationFrame() 回调你的代码。

title.en: Run as fast as you can: no control
title.zh: 尽可能快地跑：无法控制速度

subsection.en: Run, run as fast as you can

body.en: The simplest loop just calls processInput(), update(), and render() repeatedly. You have no control over how fast it runs: on a fast machine it spins too fast to follow, on a slow machine it crawls, and content-heavy parts of the game actually play slower.
body.zh: 最简单的循环只是反复调用 processInput()、update() 和 render()。你无法控制它运行的速度：在快的机器上它快得让人看不清，在慢的机器上它慢如蜗牛，而且内容繁重的场景实际上会玩得更慢。

title.en: Take a nap: sleep to a fixed frame rate
title.zh: 小睡一会儿：用 sleep 锁定帧率

body.en: For 60 FPS you have about 16 ms per frame (1000 ms / FPS). Process the frame, then sleep until it's time for the next one. This keeps the game from running too fast, but doesn't help if it runs too slowly: if a frame takes longer than 16 ms the game simply slows down.
body.zh: 要达到 60 FPS，每帧大约有 16 毫秒（1000 毫秒 / FPS）。处理完一帧后，就睡眠到下一帧该开始的时刻。这能防止游戏跑得太快，但对跑得太慢无能为力：如果一帧耗时超过 16 毫秒，游戏就会直接变慢。

subsection.en: One small step, one giant step

body.en: Choose the time step based on how much real time passed since the last frame, and pass that elapsed time to update(). Longer frames mean bigger steps, so the game always keeps up with real time; a bullet's velocity is scaled by elapsed time and crosses the screen in the same real time whether in twenty small steps or four big ones.
body.zh: 根据自上一帧以来经过的真实时间来决定时间步长，并把这段经过的时间传给 update()。帧耗时越长，步子就越大，所以游戏总能跟上真实时间；子弹的速度乘以经过的时间，无论是二十个小步还是四个大步，它都会在相同的真实时间内飞过屏幕。

title.en: Why variable steps are non-deterministic and unstable
title.zh: 为什么可变步长不确定且不稳定

subsection.en: One small step, one giant step

body.en: A deterministic program gives the same outputs for the same inputs. With variable steps, a fast machine updates a bullet 50 times while a slow one updates it 5 times, so floating-point rounding errors accumulate differently and the bullet ends up in different places. Physics engines also rely on damping tuned to a particular time step; vary it and the physics can literally blow up.
body.zh: 确定性的程序在相同输入下总是给出相同输出。使用可变步长时，快机器可能把子弹更新 50 次，而慢机器只更新 5 次，浮点舍入误差的累积因此不同，子弹最终会停在不同的位置。此外，物理引擎依赖针对特定时间步长调校的阻尼（damping）；步长一变，物理模拟就可能真的“爆炸”。

title.en: Play catch up: fixed update, variable render
title.zh: 追赶时间：固定步长更新，可变渲染

body.en: Rendering captures an instant and doesn't care how much time passed, so update with a fixed time step but render flexibly. Each frame, add the elapsed real time to a lag variable, then run update() in fixed MS_PER_UPDATE steps until the game clock catches up, and render once. The game simulates at a constant rate on any hardware; only the visible output gets choppier on slow machines.
body.zh: 渲染只捕捉某一瞬间，并不关心过去了多少时间，所以可以用固定时间步长更新，而灵活地安排渲染。每帧把经过的真实时间累加到 lag 变量上，然后以固定的 MS_PER_UPDATE 步长反复调用 update()，直到游戏时钟追上真实时间，再渲染一次。这样游戏在任何硬件上都以恒定速率模拟，只是在慢机器上画面会更卡顿。

body.en: MS_PER_UPDATE is no longer the visible frame rate, just the granularity of updates. Make it short (often faster than 60 FPS) for high fidelity, but it must be longer than the time update() takes on the slowest hardware, or the game can never catch up. You can also bail out of the inner loop after a maximum number of iterations so the game slows down rather than locking up.
body.zh: MS_PER_UPDATE 不再是可见的帧率，而只是更新的粒度。为了高保真度应让它尽量短（通常快于 60 FPS），但它必须大于最慢硬件上执行一次 update() 所需的时间，否则游戏永远追不上。你还可以让内层循环在达到最大迭代次数后退出，这样游戏只会变慢，而不会彻底卡死。

body.en: Since rendering happens at arbitrary times, it often falls between two updates, making motion look stuttery. The leftover lag tells exactly how far into the next update we are, so pass the normalized value lag / MS_PER_UPDATE (0 to just under 1) to render(). The renderer draws objects extrapolated by that fraction; the guess is sometimes wrong, but less noticeable than stutter.
body.zh: 由于渲染发生在任意时刻，它经常落在两次更新之间，导致运动看起来一顿一顿的。剩余的 lag 恰好表明我们已进入下一次更新多远，所以把归一化后的 lag / MS_PER_UPDATE（从 0 到略小于 1）传给 render()。渲染器按这个比例外推物体的位置来绘制；这种猜测有时会出错，但比卡顿更不易察觉。

title.en: Who owns the loop: platform, engine, or you?
title.zh: 谁掌控循环：平台、引擎还是你自己？

subsection.en: Do you own the game loop, or does the platform?
subsection.zh: 游戏循环由你掌控，还是由平台掌控？

body.en: Using the platform's event loop is simple and plays nice with the platform, but you lose control over timing and such loops are often slow and choppy. Using an engine's loop saves you from writing tricky code but costs flexibility. Writing your own gives total control, but you must explicitly hand control to the platform periodically so it doesn't hang.
body.zh: 使用平台的事件循环简单，且能与平台和谐共处，但你失去了对时间的控制，而且这类循环通常又慢又卡。使用引擎的循环可以省去编写棘手代码的麻烦，但会失去灵活性。自己编写则拥有完全的控制权，但你必须定期把控制权显式交还给平台，避免它挂起。

subsection.en: How do you manage power consumption?

body.en: On phones and laptops, power matters. Running as fast as possible (typical for PC games) spends all spare cycles on FPS and fidelity but uses as much power as it can. Clamping the frame rate (usually 30 or 60 FPS) sleeps for the rest of each frame, giving a "good enough" experience while sparing the battery.
body.zh: 在手机和笔记本上，电量很重要。尽可能快地运行（PC 游戏的常见做法）会把所有空闲周期都用于提高帧率和画质，但也会尽可能多地耗电。限制帧率（通常为 30 或 60 FPS）则会在每帧剩余的时间里休眠，在提供“足够好”的体验的同时节省电量。

title.en: Four ways to control gameplay speed
title.zh: 控制游戏速度的四种方式

subsection.en: How do you control gameplay speed?

body.en: Fixed step with no synchronization is simple but speed depends directly on hardware. Fixed step with synchronization is power-friendly and never too fast, but can play too slowly. Variable time step adapts both ways but is non-deterministic and unstable. Fixed update step with variable rendering is the most complex but the most adaptable: it drops rendering frames to keep up and is smoother on fast machines.
body.zh: 无同步的固定步长很简单，但速度直接受硬件影响。带同步的固定步长省电且不会过快，但可能过慢。可变时间步长能同时适应快与慢，但不确定且不稳定。固定更新步长加可变渲染最复杂，但适应性最强：它通过丢弃渲染帧来跟上进度，并在快机器上提供更流畅的体验。

body.en: The classic article on game loops is Glenn Fiedler's "Fix Your Timestep", followed closely by Witters' article on game loops. The Unity framework's complex game loop is also documented in a detailed illustration.
body.zh: 关于游戏循环的经典文章是 Glenn Fiedler 的《Fix Your Timestep》，Witters 关于游戏循环的文章紧随其后。Unity 框架的复杂游戏循环也有一张详细的图解可供参考。

exercises.q: What is the first key thing that distinguishes a game loop from a GUI event loop? 游戏循环与事件循环最关键的区别是什么？
options: 它只在空闲事件中更新游戏
It processes user input but doesn't wait for it（处理输入但不等待输入）
exercises.explain: Games keep moving even without input. 游戏在没有输入时也要继续运行，所以循环不能阻塞在输入上。

exercises.q: With a library, you own the main loop; an ___ owns the loop and calls into your code.
exercises.explain: 作者认为这是“引擎”与“库”的区别。An engine owns the loop.

exercises.q: 回合制游戏（turn-based game）不需要游戏循环，因为游戏状态只在玩家行动后才推进。
exercises.explain: False. Animation and music keep running while the game waits for your turn. 等待时视觉和音效仍在变化。

exercises.q: On Windows, which call lets your own game loop handle OS events without blocking? 哪个函数不会阻塞？
exercises.explain: PeekMessage() returns immediately, unlike GetMessage(). requestAnimationFrame() 是浏览器中的回调方式。

exercises.q: To run at 60 FPS, each frame has roughly ___ milliseconds（1000 ms / FPS）。
exercises.explain: 1000 / 60 ≈ 16.7 ms。如果一帧处理超过这个时间，sleep 版本的循环就会变慢。

exercises.q: Why does the author reject the variable time step? 作者为什么不推荐可变时间步长？
options: 它会让游戏在快机器上跑得太快
It makes the game non-deterministic and physics unstable（不确定且物理不稳定）
exercises.explain: Floating-point error accumulates differently on different machines, and damping is tuned to one step size. 浮点误差累积不同，阻尼依赖固定步长。

exercises.q: In the "play catch up" loop, MS_PER_UPDATE should be shorter than the time it takes to run update() on the slowest hardware.
exercises.explain: 错误。时间步长必须大于最慢硬件上一次 update() 的耗时，否则游戏永远追不上真实时间。

exercises.q: To smooth motion between updates, the loop calls render(lag / ___), passing a value from 0 to just under 1.
exercises.explain: 除以 MS_PER_UPDATE 进行归一化，渲染器无需关心帧率，只需按 0~1 之间的比例外推位置。

exercises.q: 解释“fixed update time step, variable rendering”循环的工作方式，以及它为什么比可变步长更好。Explain briefly in both languages.
exercises.answer: EN: Each frame it adds elapsed real time to lag, then calls update() in fixed MS_PER_UPDATE steps until lag drops below one step, then renders once. Because updates always use the same step, simulation is deterministic and physics stays stable; only rendering frames are dropped on slow machines. 中：每帧把经过的真实时间累加到 lag，然后以固定步长反复 update() 直到 lag 小于一个步长，再渲染一次。更新步长恒定，所以模拟是确定的、物理稳定；慢机器上只是丢弃渲染帧，画面更卡而已。
exercises.explain: 关键词：lag、fixed time step（固定步长）、decouple update from render（更新与渲染分离）。

exercises.q: Mobile games often clamp the frame rate to 30 or 60 FPS. 主要目的是什么？
options: To save battery by sleeping when the frame's work is done（省电）
为了避免与浏览器事件循环冲突
exercises.explain: Clamping gives a "good enough" experience and sleeps for the rest of the frame. 限制帧率后，剩余时间休眠以节省电量。

exercises.q: List one pro and one con of writing your own game loop instead of using the platform's event loop. 用中英文回答。
exercises.answer: EN: Pro — total control, designed for your game's needs. Con — you must interface with the platform, periodically handing control back so the framework doesn't hang. 中：优点是完全掌控、可为游戏量身设计；缺点是必须与平台打交道，定期交还控制权以免框架挂起或混乱。
exercises.explain: 对比：使用平台循环简单但失去时间控制；使用引擎循环省事但不够灵活。
